IMG Worldwide, Inc., 360 F.Supp.2d 681, 687 (E.D.Pa.2005) (finding that a party’s engaging in motion practice and providing “substantial discovery” constituted waiver of contractual alternative dispute resolution provision).

12	International ACH and Wire Transactions If your Account receives incoming ACH transactions (either credits or debits) or wire transfers initiated from outside of the United States, both you and we are subject to the Operating Rules and Guidelines of the National Automated Clearing House Association (“NACHA”) or the rules of any wire transfer system involved, and the laws enforced by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”). 18	The more significant problem with Love-joy’s argument that it had an “unfettered” right to redefine the House Accounts is that this interpretation would nullify portions of the Agreement’s termination provision. PL’s Opp. Br. at 17. Under the termination provision, the Agreement became effective January 1, 2004, and:
19	shall continue in force for a one (1) year period, and shall be automatically renewed for additional one (1) year periods thereafter unless terminated by written notice from either party to the other party not less than sixty (60) days prior to the end of the initial or any subsequent one (1) year term.

Id. Finally, the Agreement expressly contemplates that the parties could terminate the Agreement at any time by “mutual written agreement.” Id.
21	The termination provision, on its face, provides a comprehensive account of the ways in which the Agreement may be terminated. There is no indication in the Agreement that the parties contemplated that the House Accounts provision would constitute an additional means for terminating all of Lovejoy’s obligations under the Agreement. Under Lovejoy’s construction of the House Accounts provision, however, Lovejoy could, at any time and without Kamco’s consent, redefine every single account in Kamco’s territory as a House Account. This interpretation would allow Lovejoy to escape from all of its obligations under the Agreement and all of the restrictions in the termination provision.
22	This reading is inconsistent with Pennsylvania law, which, as noted above, forbids courts from “interpreting] one provision of a contract in a manner which results in another portion being annulled,” LJL Transp., 962 A.2d at 648 (citation omitted), and requires that “[t]he whole instrument ... be taken together in arriving at contractual intent,” Duquesne Univ., 777 A.2d at 429 (citation omitted). For example, the termination provision permits the parties to terminate the agreement at any time by “mutual written agreement.” Agreement ¶ 16. Lovejoy’s interpretation of the House Accounts provision, however, would allow it — without obtaining Kamco’s consent— to terminate all of its obligations under the Agreement at any time simply by redefining all of Kamco’s accounts as House Accounts. In other words, the “mutual” termination provision would never apply to Lovejoy.
23	Similarly, Lovejoy’s reading of the House Accounts provision would allow it to escape the effects of the 60 day notice requirement, under which the Agreement automatically renews for a full year unless either party provides notice of its intention to terminate the Agreement 60 days before the end of an annual term. Id. The evident purpose of this provision is to permit both parties to make business plans in reliance on the contract’s continued existence for a one year period. This purpose would obviously be frustrated if one party maintained a unilateral right to opt out of all of its obligations under the contract at any time — which is precisely how Lovejoy construes the House Accounts provision.
24	This court’s conclusion that Lovejoy’s reading of the House Accounts provision is inconsistent with the parties’ intent is reinforced by the fact that the Agreement contains a non-compete provision. The noncompetition provision states that Kamco could not, without Lovejoy’s permission, sell any product which is directly competitive with any Lovejoy product that Kamco was supposed to sell on Lovejoy’s behalf. Id. ¶ 2. If, as Lovejoy suggests, the House Accounts provision granted Lovejoy the “unfettered” right to redefine all or substantially all accounts as House Accounts, then Lovejoy would have the unilateral power to deprive Kamco of all of the benefits it was to receive under the contract while simultaneously barring Kamco from selling any product made by a Lovejoy competitor. Reading the House Accounts provision in this manner allows the termination provision to have its intended effect: If one of the parties wishes to put an end to its obligations to the other party, it must follow one of the enumerated ways of terminating the Agreement.

{"clause_id": "c175", "reasoning_cat1": "The warranty exclusions—'improper or insufficient maintenance, improper operation, or normal wear and tear and normal usage'—are evaluative and frequently litigated.", "reasoning_cat2": "In this cost-plus contract 7.7.3 makes the cost of correcting non-negligent nonconforming Work reimbursable, so who pays for warranty correction is not settled by the warranty alone; 12.2.2 supplies the correction period.", "prob_cat1": 0.26, "prob_cat2": 0.31},
{"clause_id": "c176", "reasoning_cat1": "A short tax-payment obligation keyed to taxes enacted or effective when bids are received or negotiations concluded.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 7.6.2 makes sales, use and similar taxes a reimbursable Cost of the Work and Exhibit D treats the Hawaii general excise tax as a job cost calculated on direct costs, so the Contractor 'pays' but the Owner funds—two different allocations.", "prob_cat1": 0.13, "prob_cat2": 0.34},
{"clause_id": "c177", "reasoning_cat1": "'Customarily secured after execution of the Contract' and 'legally required when bids are received or negotiations concluded' are timing qualifiers that could be argued but are standard.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 7.6.3 makes permit fees reimbursable, and revised 4.1 makes commencement itself 'pending approval of permits,' so permit responsibility and timing are addressed in three places.", "prob_cat1": 0.11, "prob_cat2": 0.29},
{"clause_id": "c178", "reasoning_cat1": "A general compliance obligation, plainly stated.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 3.7.3, 3.7.4 and Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1.", "prob_cat1": 0.06, "prob_cat2": 0.08},
{"clause_id": "c179", "reasoning_cat1": "Disclaims a duty to ascertain legal conformity but imposes a duty to report observed variances—an interplay that is stated clearly.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 requires compliance with the more stringent of the documents and applicable codes, which presses beyond mere reporting.", "prob_cat1": 0.11, "prob_cat2": 0.17},
{"clause_id": "c180", "reasoning_cat1": "'Knowing it to be contrary' sets a scienter test; clear enough.", "reasoning_cat2": "Fits with 3.7.3 and with 8.1.6's exclusion of costs due to the Contractor's failure to fulfil responsibilities.", "prob_cat1": 0.10, "prob_cat2": 0.15},
{"clause_id": "c181", "reasoning_cat1": "Straightforward requirement to include stated allowances in the Contract Sum.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 5.2.4 states no allowances and the Contract Sum here is Cost of the Work plus Fee rather than a fixed price, so the allowance machinery has little to bite on.", "prob_cat1": 0.09, "prob_cat2": 0.29},

{"clause_id": "c168", "reasoning_cat1": "A two-notice cure procedure with a defined Change Order remedy; internally clear.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 2.4.1 [Revision] deletes the second notice and shortens the procedure, while the Supplementary Conditions preamble says unaltered General Conditions provisions remain in effect—so two cure regimes coexist.", "prob_cat1": 0.10, "prob_cat2": 0.44},

{"clause_id": "c171", "reasoning_cat1": "A non-waiver provision in standard terms.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 4.2.3 and 9.6.6; no conflict.", "prob_cat1": 0.08, "prob_cat2": 0.08},
{"clause_id": "c172", "reasoning_cat1": "The clause simultaneously requires careful study and disclaims that the review is 'for the purpose of discovering errors, omissions, or inconsistencies,' a tension litigants regularly exploit.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1(b) makes the Contractor responsible for the correctness of field measurements with 'no extra charge,' and 1.2.1.1 requires the more stringent requirement, which cuts against the limited-purpose disclaimer here.", "prob_cat1": 0.23, "prob_cat2": 0.31},
{"clause_id": "c173", "reasoning_cat1": "Distinguishes the Contractor's contractor-capacity review from design responsibility; the boundary is stated but inherently blurry.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 requires shop drawings prepared by trade experts and, where required, a licensed engineer, edging the Contractor toward design responsibility.", "prob_cat1": 0.16, "prob_cat2": 0.21},
{"clause_id": "c174", "reasoning_cat1": "Preserves claims for cost or time from clarifications while imposing damages for failure to report; the two limbs are dense but stated.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 permits increases only by Change Order and bars unjust-enrichment claims, and 1.2.1.1(b) allows 'no extra charge' for dimensional differences; the claim right here must be squared with both.", "prob_cat1": 0.21, "prob_cat2": 0.35},
{"clause_id": "c175", "reasoning_cat1": "The warranty exclusions—'improper or insufficient maintenance, improper operation, or normal wear and tear and normal usage'—are evaluative and frequently litigated.", "reasoning_cat2": "In this cost-plus contract 7.7.3 makes the cost of correcting non-negligent nonconforming Work reimbursable, so who pays for warranty correction is not settled by the warranty alone; 12.2.2 supplies the correction period.", "prob_cat1": 0.26, "prob_cat2": 0.31},
{"clause_id": "c176", "reasoning_cat1": "A short tax-payment obligation keyed to taxes enacted or effective when bids are received or negotiations concluded.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 7.6.2 makes sales, use and similar taxes a reimbursable Cost of the Work and Exhibit D treats the Hawaii general excise tax as a job cost calculated on direct costs, so the Contractor 'pays' but the Owner funds—two different allocations.", "prob_cat1": 0.13, "prob_cat2": 0.34},
{"clause_id": "c177", "reasoning_cat1": "'Customarily secured after execution of the Contract' and 'legally required when bids are received or negotiations concluded' are timing qualifiers that could be argued but are standard.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 7.6.3 makes permit fees reimbursable, and revised 4.1 makes commencement itself 'pending approval of permits,' so permit responsibility and timing are addressed in three places.", "prob_cat1": 0.11, "prob_cat2": 0.29},
{"clause_id": "c178", "reasoning_cat1": "A general compliance obligation, plainly stated.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 3.7.3, 3.7.4 and Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1.", "prob_cat1": 0.06, "prob_cat2": 0.08},
{"clause_id": "c179", "reasoning_cat1": "Disclaims a duty to ascertain legal conformity but imposes a duty to report observed variances—an interplay that is stated clearly.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 1.2.1.1 requires compliance with the more stringent of the documents and applicable codes, which presses beyond mere reporting.", "prob_cat1": 0.11, "prob_cat2": 0.17},
{"clause_id": "c180", "reasoning_cat1": "'Knowing it to be contrary' sets a scienter test; clear enough.", "reasoning_cat2": "Fits with 3.7.3 and with 8.1.6's exclusion of costs due to the Contractor's failure to fulfil responsibilities.", "prob_cat1": 0.10, "prob_cat2": 0.15},
{"clause_id": "c181", "reasoning_cat1": "Straightforward requirement to include stated allowances in the Contract Sum.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 5.2.4 states no allowances and the Contract Sum here is Cost of the Work plus Fee rather than a fixed price, so the allowance machinery has little to bite on.", "prob_cat1": 0.09, "prob_cat2": 0.29},

{"clause_id": "c202", "reasoning_cat1": "'Arising out of or resulting from performance of the Work,' 'but only to the extent caused by the negligent acts or omissions,' and the survival of other indemnity rights are the standard battlegrounds of construction indemnity litigation.", "reasoning_cat2": "The indemnity is expressly limited to claims 'not covered by Project Management Protective Liability insurance purchased by the Contractor in accordance with Paragraph 11.3,' which is optional and which Article 16 (blank) never required; it also sits against the 4.3.10 consequential waiver and 11.4.7 subrogation waivers.", "prob_cat1": 0.26, "prob_cat2": 0.29},
{"clause_id": "c203", "reasoning_cat1": "A short anti-limitation rule for workers' compensation defences; clearly expressed.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supports 3.18.1; no contrary provision found.", "prob_cat1": 0.14, "prob_cat2": 0.13},
{"clause_id": "c204", "reasoning_cat1": "Definitional; nothing to construe.", "reasoning_cat2": "The Architect is identified in the Agreement; consistent.", "prob_cat1": 0.06, "prob_cat2": 0.10},
{"clause_id": "c205", "reasoning_cat1": "A single rule requiring the written consent of Owner, Contractor and Architect to change the Architect's duties.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 subjects every Architect approval to the Owner's express concurrence and Agreement 12.2.3 supersedes A201 9.4.1's timing—modifications of the Architect's authority made without any recorded Architect consent.", "prob_cat1": 0.11, "prob_cat2": 0.42},
{"clause_id": "c206", "reasoning_cat1": "The transcription is badly garbled, but the substance—a successor architect with the former Architect's status, subject to reasonable objection—is standard.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 4.1.2 and the Agreement's identification of the Architect.", "prob_cat1": 0.15, "prob_cat2": 0.11},
{"clause_id": "c207", "reasoning_cat1": "Describes the Architect's administration role and limits authority to what the Contract Documents provide; clear.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 adds an Owner consent layer to every Architect function, so the Architect's role as 'Owner's representative' is doubled up.", "prob_cat1": 0.10, "prob_cat2": 0.21},
{"clause_id": "c208", "reasoning_cat1": "A disclaimer of Architect responsibility in conventional terms.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 3.1.3 and 4.2.2; no conflict.", "prob_cat1": 0.08, "prob_cat2": 0.10},
{"clause_id": "c209", "reasoning_cat1": "'Shall endeavor to communicate ... through the Architect' is hortatory rather than mandatory, which itself invites argument about notices.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 requires direct written notice to and consent of the Owner wherever the Architect is involved, and 2.1.1.1 names Owner decision-makers, so routing of communications is stated two different ways.", "prob_cat1": 0.14, "prob_cat2": 0.34},
{"clause_id": "c210", "reasoning_cat1": "The transcription is fragmentary but the function—evaluate applications and certify amounts due—is standard.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 12.2.3 expressly supersedes A201 9.4.1's time periods for final certification, and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 adds a precondition to the final Certificate.", "prob_cat1": 0.11, "prob_cat2": 0.22},
{"clause_id": "c211", "reasoning_cat1": "A long, carefully limited description of review 'only for the limited purpose of checking for conformance'; length is not ambiguity.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 3.12.7.1 requires Architect approval of all shop drawings, which fits within this review limitation.", "prob_cat1": 0.15, "prob_cat2": 0.15},
{"clause_id": "c212", "reasoning_cat1": "A short statement of the Architect's Change Order authority.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 makes the Change Order the only route to a change in Contract Sum or Time except under 7.3 and 9.7.1, which narrows the minor-changes authority referenced here.", "prob_cat1": 0.07, "prob_cat2": 0.21},
{"clause_id": "c213", "reasoning_cat1": "Badly transcribed, but the function—determining Substantial Completion and issuing the final Certificate—is standard.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 bars the final Certificate until the Owner accepts all warranties, and Agreement 12.2.3 sets a different certification timetable.", "prob_cat1": 0.11, "prob_cat2": 0.26},
{"clause_id": "c214", "reasoning_cat1": "Conditional on agreement between Owner and Architect; nothing to construe.", "reasoning_cat2": "No project representatives are identified in the Contract Documents, so the provision is dormant.", "prob_cat1": 0.08, "prob_cat2": 0.11},
{"clause_id": "c215", "reasoning_cat1": "The 15-day rule for recognising delay is precise, though 'reasonable promptness' governs in the first instance.", "reasoning_cat2": "Works with 4.2.12 and 4.4.1; Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 adds Owner concurrence to interpretations.", "prob_cat1": 0.15, "prob_cat2": 0.20},
{"clause_id": "c216", "reasoning_cat1": "'Consistent with the intent of and reasonably inferable from the Contract Documents' repeats the elastic standard of 1.2.1, and good-faith immunity is broad.", "reasoning_cat2": "It coexists with 4.4's claim procedure and Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1's Owner-concurrence requirement without direct contradiction.", "prob_cat1": 0.16, "prob_cat2": 0.16},
{"clause_id": "c217", "reasoning_cat1": "Finality is granted and then qualified in the same sentence ('will be final if consistent with the intent expressed in the Contract Documents'), and 'aesthetic effect' is undefined.", "reasoning_cat2": "4.5.1 and 4.6.1 exclude aesthetic-effect claims from mediation and arbitration, while Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 reserves aesthetic control to the Owner—so who decides aesthetics, and where, is genuinely unsettled.", "prob_cat1": 0.31, "prob_cat2": 0.31},
{"clause_id": "c218", "reasoning_cat1": "A definition covering demands, assertions and 'other disputes and matters in question'; broad but deliberately so.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 4.4-4.6 and with Agreement 12.2.4's separate arbitration right.", "prob_cat1": 0.12, "prob_cat2": 0.13},
{"clause_id": "c219", "reasoning_cat1": "The 21-day trigger is stated twice with a 'whichever is later' rule, but the clause never says whether compliance is a condition precedent to recovery.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 4.3.7.3 imposes further content requirements, Agreement 12.2.4 sets its own 30-day rule, and 4.3.4 has a parallel 21-day period; the notice regime is layered.", "prob_cat1": 0.21, "prob_cat2": 0.27},
{"clause_id": "c220", "reasoning_cat1": "A clear duty to continue performance and payment pending resolution, with two stated exceptions.", "reasoning_cat2": "It requires the Owner to 'continue to make payments' while 9.5.1 permits withholding certification and 12.1.7.5-.6 permit deductions, so the reach of the duty depends on those provisions.", "prob_cat1": 0.11, "prob_cat2": 0.25},
{"clause_id": "c221", "reasoning_cat1": "'Differ materially,' 'unknown physical conditions of an unusual nature,' and 'generally recognized as inherent in construction activities of the character provided for' are the classic differing-site-conditions phrases.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 allows Contract Sum changes only by Change Order, 1.2.1.1(b) allows no extra charge for dimensional differences, and in a cost-plus contract costs flow through anyway—three inconsistent treatments of extra cost.", "prob_cat1": 0.32, "prob_cat2": 0.34},
{"clause_id": "c222", "reasoning_cat1": "'For reasons including but not limited to' followed by six enumerated grounds is precisely the general-versus-specific structure that generates ejusdem generis arguments.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 bars increases except by Change Order and the Agreement's cost-plus structure already passes cost through, so the claim grounds here need reconciling.", "prob_cat1": 0.29, "prob_cat2": 0.26},
{"clause_id": "c223", "reasoning_cat1": "Requires written notice and an estimate of cost and probable effect; clear.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Conditions 4.3.7.3 and 4.3.7.4 add detailed content requirements and a concurrent-delay bar, which supplement rather than contradict.", "prob_cat1": 0.12, "prob_cat2": 0.21},
{"clause_id": "c224", "reasoning_cat1": "'Abnormal for the period of time' and 'could not have been reasonably anticipated' are evaluative tests that regularly produce disputes about weather claims.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 4.3.7.4's concurrent-delay bar interacts with weather claims, but there is no contradiction.", "prob_cat1": 0.28, "prob_cat2": 0.20},
{"clause_id": "c225", "reasoning_cat1": "'Within a reasonable time not exceeding 21 days' fixes an outer limit; the drafting is clear.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 4.3.2 and the insurance articles.", "prob_cat1": 0.12, "prob_cat2": 0.10},
{"clause_id": "c226", "reasoning_cat1": "'Materially changed' and 'substantial inequity' are soft, but the remedy (equitable adjustment) is standard.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 5.2.3 states no unit prices, so the provision operates only on prices 'subsequently agreed upon.'", "prob_cat1": 0.14, "prob_cat2": 0.24},
{"clause_id": "c227", "reasoning_cat1": "The waiver's boundary—waived consequential damages including 'loss of profit except anticipated profit arising directly from the Work,' with liquidated direct damages preserved—is a much-litigated line.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 13.1 lets the Contractor recover a fee computed as if the Work were fully completed and A201 14.1.3 allows 'reasonable overhead, profit and damages,' which press against the waiver of profit and of termination-related consequential damages.", "prob_cat1": 0.30, "prob_cat2": 0.33},
{"clause_id": "c228", "reasoning_cat1": "A menu of five permitted actions within ten days; precise, apart from the Architect's 'sole discretion' escape.", "reasoning_cat2": "Fits 4.4.1 and 4.4.5; Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 adds Owner involvement.", "prob_cat1": 0.11, "prob_cat2": 0.15},
{"clause_id": "c229", "reasoning_cat1": "Permissive consultation with a cost-allocation sentence; clear.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 4.4.2 and 7.6.8's treatment of professional costs.", "prob_cat1": 0.10, "prob_cat2": 0.10},
{"clause_id": "c230", "reasoning_cat1": "A ten-day response requirement with three permitted responses; definite.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 4.4.2 and 4.4.5.", "prob_cat1": 0.10, "prob_cat2": 0.10},
{"clause_id": "c231", "reasoning_cat1": "Written decision, reasons, and 'final and binding ... but subject to mediation and arbitration' is an internally odd but well-understood formulation.", "reasoning_cat2": "It interacts with 4.4.6's 30-day demand rule and with Agreement 12.2.4, which permits arbitration without a further Architect decision.", "prob_cat1": 0.15, "prob_cat2": 0.18},
{"clause_id": "c232", "reasoning_cat1": "The consequence of failing to demand arbitration within 30 days is stated, though the condition ('when a written decision ... states that') makes the trigger depend on the Architect's drafting.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 12.2.4 imposes a separate 30-day demand rule for final-accounting disputes and 4.6.3 adds a further limit, so three time bars operate on overlapping claims.", "prob_cat1": 0.21, "prob_cat2": 0.29},
{"clause_id": "c233", "reasoning_cat1": "Purely permissive notice to the surety.", "reasoning_cat2": "No surety or bond is required by Article 16, so the provision is largely dormant.", "prob_cat1": 0.08, "prob_cat2": 0.12},
{"clause_id": "c234", "reasoning_cat1": "A short lien-preservation rule; clear.", "reasoning_cat2": "Interacts with Addendum 12.1.4(b) lien waivers and revised 12.2.2's lien-free endorsement condition, but consistently.", "prob_cat1": 0.12, "prob_cat2": 0.19},
{"clause_id": "c235", "reasoning_cat1": "Badly transcribed but substantively the standard AAA mediation procedure with a 60-day stay of arbitration.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 12.2.4 lets the Contractor demand arbitration of the final-accounting dispute directly, which sits against 4.5.1's condition precedent.", "prob_cat1": 0.16, "prob_cat2": 0.26},
{"clause_id": "c236", "reasoning_cat1": "Fee sharing, venue and enforceability of settlements; all definite.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 13.1.1 governing law; no conflict.", "prob_cat1": 0.06, "prob_cat2": 0.10},
{"clause_id": "c237", "reasoning_cat1": "The exceptions (aesthetic effect and the 4.3.10, 9.10.4-9.10.5 waivers) are cross-referenced rather than described, and the transcription is fragmentary.", "reasoning_cat2": "Aesthetic claims are excluded here and made 'final' by 4.2.13 subject to a consistency proviso, while Agreement 12.2.4 permits arbitration outside this route; the dispute architecture is not fully harmonised.", "prob_cat1": 0.19, "prob_cat2": 0.33},
{"clause_id": "c238", "reasoning_cat1": "Identifies the rules and the filing requirements precisely.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 12.2.4's demand mechanism and 4.4.6's time limit interlock with this; no contradiction in the filing mechanics.", "prob_cat1": 0.10, "prob_cat2": 0.20},
{"clause_id": "c239", "reasoning_cat1": "The outer limit—no demand after the date when legal proceedings 'would be barred by the applicable statute of limitations as determined pursuant to Paragraph 13.7'—stacks three cross-references and is hard to apply.", "reasoning_cat2": "13.7.1 fixes accrual dates by project milestone and 4.4.6 and Agreement 12.2.4 add 30-day bars, so the limitation scheme has several moving parts.", "prob_cat1": 0.26, "prob_cat2": 0.25},
{"clause_id": "c240", "reasoning_cat1": "A dense series of negatives about consolidation and joinder, turning on phrases such as 'substantially involved in a common question of fact or law whose presence is required if complete relief is to be accorded.'", "reasoning_cat2": "The Architect is not a party to the Agreement yet performs decisive functions, and Agreement 12.2.4 contemplates arbitration of accounting disputes; joinder questions therefore arise naturally.", "prob_cat1": 0.30, "prob_cat2": 0.24},
{"clause_id": "c241", "reasoning_cat1": "A one-sentence enforcement provision.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 4.6.2 and 13.1.1.", "prob_cat1": 0.06, "prob_cat2": 0.09},
{"clause_id": "c242", "reasoning_cat1": "Definitional; the exclusion of separate contractors is express.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with Agreement Article 10 and A201 6.1.2.", "prob_cat1": 0.06, "prob_cat2": 0.09},
{"clause_id": "c243", "reasoning_cat1": "Definitional; nothing to construe.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 5.3.1 flow-down requirements.", "prob_cat1": 0.05, "prob_cat2": 0.06},
{"clause_id": "c244", "reasoning_cat1": "'Failure of the Owner or Architect to reply promptly shall constitute notice of no reasonable objection' converts silence into consent without defining 'promptly.'", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 10.1 gives the Owner power to designate bidders and to determine which bids are accepted, and Addendum 6.5 requires at least two bids including Owner- or Architect-named subcontractors—a materially different selection process.", "prob_cat1": 0.17, "prob_cat2": 0.34},
{"clause_id": "c245", "reasoning_cat1": "'Reasonable and timely objection' is soft but conventional, and the reciprocal right is clear.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 10.1's final sentence states the same reciprocal right, and Addendum 6.5 requires named subcontractors to be 'reasonably acceptable to Contractor.'", "prob_cat1": 0.11, "prob_cat2": 0.24},
{"clause_id": "c246", "reasoning_cat1": "The adjustment turns on whether the rejected subcontractor was 'reasonably capable of performing the Work' and on the Contractor having 'acted promptly and responsively.'", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 10.2 provides a different remedy for Owner-forced bid substitution measured by the difference in bids and adjusting the Guaranteed Maximum Price; two remedies for similar facts.", "prob_cat1": 0.16, "prob_cat2": 0.28},
{"clause_id": "c247", "reasoning_cat1": "A one-line restriction; clear.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 5.2.1-5.2.3 and Agreement 10.1.", "prob_cat1": 0.08, "prob_cat2": 0.14},
{"clause_id": "c248", "reasoning_cat1": "A contingent assignment with three conditions; the mechanism is dense but each condition is stated.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 13.3 requires the Contractor to execute assignments as a condition of receiving termination payments, and 14.2.2 lets the Owner accept assignment; the routes overlap.", "prob_cat1": 0.18, "prob_cat2": 0.27},
{"clause_id": "c249", "reasoning_cat1": "Equitable adjustment of the subcontractor's compensation after suspension; short and standard.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with Agreement 13.4 and A201 14.3.2.", "prob_cat1": 0.10, "prob_cat2": 0.12},
{"clause_id": "c250", "reasoning_cat1": "Reserves the Owner's right to self-perform or award separate contracts, with a claim route for the Contractor.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement Article 2 excepts work indicated to be others' responsibility; consistent.", "prob_cat1": 0.10, "prob_cat2": 0.12},
{"clause_id": "c251", "reasoning_cat1": "A definitional convention for multiple contracts.", "reasoning_cat2": "No separate contracts are identified; dormant but consistent.", "prob_cat1": 0.07, "prob_cat2": 0.08},
{"clause_id": "c252", "reasoning_cat1": "Coordination duties with a mechanism for revising the construction schedule by joint review and mutual agreement.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Conditions 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 make the Construction Schedule a Contract Document revised by Contractor and Architect at design phases, a different process from the joint review with separate contractors described here.", "prob_cat1": 0.13, "prob_cat2": 0.29}
]}

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id": "c253", "reasoning_cat1": "Deems the Owner subject to Contractor-like obligations when self-performing; the cross-references are specific.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 6.1.1 and 6.2; no separate contracts are identified here.", "prob_cat1": 0.08, "prob_cat2": 0.10},
{"clause_id": "c254", "reasoning_cat1": "'Reasonable opportunity' for introduction and storage is soft but conventional.", "reasoning_cat2": "Fits 6.1.3 coordination and 3.13.1 use of site.", "prob_cat1": 0.10, "prob_cat2": 0.10},
{"clause_id": "c255", "reasoning_cat1": "Failure to report is deemed an acknowledgment that other construction is fit, 'except as to defects not then reasonably discoverable'—a deeming rule with a discoverability escape that invites argument.", "reasoning_cat2": "It parallels 3.2.1's review duties and 4.3.4's concealed-conditions right without direct contradiction.", "prob_cat1": 0.22, "prob_cat2": 0.16},
{"clause_id": "c256", "reasoning_cat1": "Allocates costs of 'improperly timed activities, damage to the Work or defective construction' both ways; the categories are stated.", "reasoning_cat2": "Reads with 4.3.6 claim grounds and Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1's Change Order requirement.", "prob_cat1": 0.15, "prob_cat2": 0.17},
{"clause_id": "c257", "reasoning_cat1": "'Damage wrongfully caused' imports a fault standard that the clause does not define.", "reasoning_cat2": "Cross-refers to 10.2.5, which uses a different (causation-and-responsibility) formula; the two sit together loosely.", "prob_cat1": 0.18, "prob_cat2": 0.14},
{"clause_id": "c258", "reasoning_cat1": "A one-line equivalence rule.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 3.14 and 6.1.4.", "prob_cat1": 0.06, "prob_cat2": 0.09},
{"clause_id": "c259", "reasoning_cat1": "A dispute-triggered self-help and cost-allocation rule; clear.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 3.15 and 7.5.3's reimbursement of debris removal.", "prob_cat1": 0.10, "prob_cat2": 0.12},
{"clause_id": "c260", "reasoning_cat1": "Lists the three instruments by which changes may be made, 'subject to the limitations stated in this Article 7 and elsewhere in the Contract Documents.'", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 narrows this to Change Orders except under 7.3 and 9.7.1, and Addendum 6.5 adds a fast-track Change Order procedure.", "prob_cat1": 0.11, "prob_cat2": 0.25},
{"clause_id": "c261", "reasoning_cat1": "A precise definition requiring preparation by the Architect and signature by Owner, Contractor and Architect.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1 makes the Change Order the sole route to a Contract Sum change while Addendum 6.5 contemplates Change Orders issued as items are priced; the signature formalities are not repeated there.", "prob_cat1": 0.12, "prob_cat2": 0.29},
{"clause_id": "c262", "reasoning_cat1": "A fragmentary cross-reference to the permitted methods of adjustment.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 6.1-6.3 override the meaning of 'cost' and 'fee' in these methods, which is an express reconciliation.", "prob_cat1": 0.10, "prob_cat2": 0.20},

{"clause_id": "c289", "reasoning_cat1": "Payment 'in the manner and within the time provided in the Contract Documents'—an entirely referential obligation.", "reasoning_cat2": "The referenced timing is in Agreement 12.1.3, whose day numerals are blank or illegible, and in the revised 12.2.2 for final payment; the obligation is only as definite as those.", "prob_cat1": 0.12, "prob_cat2": 0.33},
{"clause_id": "c290", "reasoning_cat1": "Prompt payment to subcontractors 'reflecting percentages actually retained' is clear in principle.", "reasoning_cat2": "Retainage in this contract is stated three ways—'N/A' in the printed 12.1.7.3, five percent in the Addendum, and not less than ten percent for subcontractors in 12.1.8—so what percentage is 'actually retained' is uncertain.", "prob_cat1": 0.13, "prob_cat2": 0.30},
{"clause_id": "c291", "reasoning_cat1": "A short disclaimer with a saving clause for legal requirements.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 9.6.2.1 allows the Owner to make joint payments while disclaiming any obligation to subcontractors, which is consistent with this.", "prob_cat1": 0.08, "prob_cat2": 0.20},
{"clause_id": "c292", "reasoning_cat1": "An equivalence rule for material suppliers.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 9.6.2 and Supplementary Condition 9.6.2.1.", "prob_cat1": 0.08, "prob_cat2": 0.10},
{"clause_id": "c293", "reasoning_cat1": "A short non-acceptance rule.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 9.9.3 and 12.3.1.", "prob_cat1": 0.06, "prob_cat2": 0.10},
{"clause_id": "c294", "reasoning_cat1": "It creates a holding obligation and then disclaims fiduciary liability, tort liability, segregation and punitive damages—an obligation stripped of most remedies, keyed to 'the full penal sum of the Contract Sum.'", "reasoning_cat2": "No Contract Sum is stated (5.1.1, 5.2.1) and Article 16 requires no payment bond, so the trigger for the holding obligation cannot be measured.", "prob_cat1": 0.21, "prob_cat2": 0.31},
{"clause_id": "c295", "reasoning_cat1": "The stop-work right and its consequences are specific, subject to the seven-day and seven-day windows.", "reasoning_cat2": "It runs from 'the date established in the Contract Documents,' which Agreement 12.1.3 leaves blank, and adds 'interest as provided for in the Contract Documents,' which 14.2 states as 'N/A.'", "prob_cat1": 0.16, "prob_cat2": 0.34},
{"clause_id": "c296", "reasoning_cat1": "'Sufficiently complete ... so that the Owner can occupy or utilize the Work for its intended use' is the most litigated standard in the form, especially where completion dates and bonuses depend on it.", "reasoning_cat2": "Revised 4.3 fixes a completion date, 4.4 pays a bonus for early substantial completion without saying who determines it, and Addendum 12.2.1 adds a recorded Notice of Completion—three milestones keyed to this definition.", "prob_cat1": 0.27, "prob_cat2": 0.30},
{"clause_id": "c297", "reasoning_cat1": "'Comprehensive list of items to be completed or corrected' with an express non-waiver; clear.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 9.8.3-9.8.5 and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1.", "prob_cat1": 0.10, "prob_cat2": 0.12},
{"clause_id": "c298", "reasoning_cat1": "The inspection standard mirrors 9.8.1's 'intended use' test; the procedure is definite.", "reasoning_cat2": "Supplementary Condition 1.1.2.1 adds Owner concurrence to Architect determinations, which affects this inspection.", "prob_cat1": 0.13, "prob_cat2": 0.17},
{"clause_id": "c299", "reasoning_cat1": "The Certificate establishes date, responsibilities and warranty commencement 'unless otherwise provided in the Certificate,' which leaves the content partly to the Architect.", "reasoning_cat2": "12.2.2.1's one-year correction period runs from Substantial Completion and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 controls warranty delivery, so the warranty timeline depends on several texts.", "prob_cat1": 0.16, "prob_cat2": 0.25},
{"clause_id": "c300", "reasoning_cat1": "Payment of retainage on acceptance and surety consent; the mechanism is stated.", "reasoning_cat2": "The retainage percentage is stated inconsistently ('N/A' in the printed 12.1.7.3, five percent in the Addendum, ten percent for subcontractors in 12.1.8), so the amount to be released is unsettled.", "prob_cat1": 0.13, "prob_cat2": 0.34},
{"clause_id": "c301", "reasoning_cat1": "A joint-inspection requirement; clear.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 9.9.1 and 11.4.1.5's insurer consent.", "prob_cat1": 0.06, "prob_cat2": 0.10},

{"clause_id": "c303", "reasoning_cat1": "The final-certificate conditions and representations are detailed and internally consistent.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 12.2.3 substitutes an accountant-driven basis and timetable for final certification, and Supplementary Condition 9.10.1.1 forbids issuance until the Owner accepts all warranties.", "prob_cat1": 0.13, "prob_cat2": 0.35},
{"clause_id": "c304", "reasoning_cat1": "Five enumerated submittals with a bond alternative for refused waivers; specific, though 'other data ... in such form as may be designated by the Owner' is open.", "reasoning_cat2": "Addendum 12.1.4(b) already requires progress lien waivers and revised 12.2.2 requires a lien-free title endorsement, so the lien-clearing obligations are cumulative across three provisions.", "prob_cat1": 0.16, "prob_cat2": 0.27}
]}

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id": "c337", "reasoning_cat1": "The waiver runs 'to the extent covered by property insurance obtained pursuant to this Paragraph 11.4 or other property insurance applicable to the Work,' a coverage-dependent boundary that is routinely fought over.", "reasoning_cat2": "The Owner's property insurance amount cannot be computed because no Contract Sum is stated (5.1.1, 5.2.1, A201 9.1.1), and Supplementary Condition 11.4.1.1.1 requires a matching waiver on the Contractor's own equipment policy.", "prob_cat1": 0.26, "prob_cat2": 0.29},
{"clause_id": "c338", "reasoning_cat1": "Adjustment by the Owner 'as fiduciary' with distribution to subcontractors; the mechanism is stated, and the cross-reference to 11.4.10 is intact in the form.", "reasoning_cat2": "Cross-refers to subparagraphs of 11.4 that are not reproduced in the enumerated provisions here, and it presupposes Owner-purchased property insurance whose amount is indeterminate.", "prob_cat1": 0.15, "prob_cat2": 0.24},
{"clause_id": "c339", "reasoning_cat1": "'Whether discovered before or after Substantial Completion' and the inclusion of testing and Architect's costs are clear allocations.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 7.7.3 (as revised by the Addendum) makes the cost of correcting damaged or nonconforming Work a reimbursable Cost of the Work when not caused by the Contractor's negligence, which pulls against 'costs ... shall be at the Contractor's expense.'", "prob_cat1": 0.19, "prob_cat2": 0.34},
{"clause_id": "c340", "reasoning_cat1": "The transcription drops words, leaving the extension formula incomplete on the face of the provision.", "reasoning_cat2": "Works with 12.2.2.1 and 9.8.4's warranty commencement; no conflict located.", "prob_cat1": 0.21, "prob_cat2": 0.15},
{"clause_id": "c341", "reasoning_cat1": "As transcribed the sentence is missing its operative words and reads as a non-sequitur about the one-year period.", "reasoning_cat2": "It is the standard companion to 12.2.2.2 and consistent with 12.2.5.", "prob_cat1": 0.24, "prob_cat2": 0.14},
{"clause_id": "c342", "reasoning_cat1": "It carefully separates the correction obligation from the limitation period, but the drafting is dense and doubly negative.", "reasoning_cat2": "13.7.1 fixes deemed accrual dates and 4.6.3 bars late arbitration demands, so the interplay of correction period and limitation is spread over three provisions.", "prob_cat1": 0.20, "prob_cat2": 0.21},
{"clause_id": "c343", "reasoning_cat1": "'The law of the place where the Project is located' is definite here, the Project being in Hawaii.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 4.5.3's venue rule and Addendum 14.6(c)'s Hawaii licensing warranty.", "prob_cat1": 0.12, "prob_cat2": 0.14},
{"clause_id": "c344", "reasoning_cat1": "Badly transcribed but substantively the standard binding-on-successors and no-assignment-without-consent rule.", "reasoning_cat2": "It cross-refers to 13.2.2 (Owner assignment to a lender), which is not among the enumerated provisions here; otherwise consistent with 5.4.1.", "prob_cat1": 0.16, "prob_cat2": 0.16},
{"clause_id": "c345", "reasoning_cat1": "Only fragments survive in the transcription, but the substance is a standard cumulative-remedies and non-waiver clause.", "reasoning_cat2": "It preserves remedies that other provisions (4.3.10 waiver, 9.10.4-9.10.5 waivers, Supplementary Condition 7.1.3.1) expressly cut back, which is a familiar tension in this form.", "prob_cat1": 0.16, "prob_cat2": 0.22},
{"clause_id": "c346", "reasoning_cat1": "The transcription is fragmentary, leaving the allocation of testing responsibility hard to read from the provision itself.", "reasoning_cat2": "Agreement 7.6.4 makes laboratory fees reimbursable except those excluded by 13.5.3, so cost allocation for tests is governed jointly by the two.", "prob_cat1": 0.19, "prob_cat2": 0.25},

{"clause_id": "c348", "reasoning_cat1": "One line requiring prompt testing to avoid delay.", "reasoning_cat2": "Consistent with 8.2 and 13.5.", "prob_cat1": 0.08, "prob_cat2": 0.08},
{"clause_id": "c349", "reasoning_cat1": "Deemed-accrual rules of this kind ('any alleged cause of action shall be deemed to have accrued in any and all events not later than ...') are much litigated, and the transcription of limb .3 is partly unreadable.", "reasoning_cat2": "4.6.3 measures the arbitration deadline by reference to this paragraph and 12.2.2 sets a one-year correction period, so accrual, correction and demand deadlines interlock.", "prob_cat1": 0.31, "prob_cat2": 0.27},
{"clause_id": "c350", "reasoning_cat1": "Four enumerated stoppage grounds with a 30-day trigger; each ground is specific.", "reasoning_cat2": "Ground .3 depends on payment 'within the time stated in the Contract Documents,' which Agreement 12.1.3 leaves blank, and Agreement 13.1 caps what the Contractor may recover on such a termination.", "prob_cat1": 0.18, "prob_cat2": 0.29},
